messages:
Maya: alerting here — eu-west-1 dedicated pool is showing slot oscillation and we've hit p99 generation latency > 900ms for tenant cust-teamX. SLA alert fired. Visible throughput drop ~22% :warning:
Trent: saw it on dashboards, looks like repeated evictions on pool-44, eviction_count spiked at 14:25 UTC
Li: quick check — are we seeing placement reshuffles? I can tail the allocation events
Maya: yes, placement events show nodes getting deallocated and reallocated for the pool. logs: `placement: affinity_mismatch -> fallback_alloc` several times
Jenna: noisy-neighbor suspicion — one host in pool-44 has bad kernel selection path, falls back to slower kernels which slows batching cadence
Trent: interesting — profiler snapshot around 14:25 shows kernel_choice thrash: rapid toggles between fused-attn and fallback-atten kernels, 60% increase in kernel selection time
Li: dumping recent node metrics: host-44b CPU jitter high, KV cache hit rate on that host dropped from 0.87 -> 0.32 in 10m
Maya: KV cache thrash could explain both latency and eviction churn. Any recent config changes to tenant quotas or placement policies?
Jenna: ops-bot shows a config roll earlier today: `dedicated.pool.affinity_weight` lowered from 0.9 -> 0.6 for eu-west rollout (PR #1247). Could cause looser affinity and more reshuffles
Trent: who deployed that PR? It was automated by the rollout manager around 13:50 UTC
Li: rolling back affinity change would rebind tenants to preferred hosts — but we need to be sure it's safe. Also need to investigate why kernel selection becomes unstable on that host
Maya: quick mitigation: can we pin cust-teamX to alternative pool or enable canary fallback to smaller-vmem models? We need to stop SLA breach ASAP
Jenna: oncall, can you trigger immediate placement override for cust-teamX to pool-47 and add placement stickiness for 30m? :point_up:
oncall: doing placement override now -> submitted `override: tenant=cust-teamX, dest_pool=pool-47, sticky_ttl=1800`
oncall: placement override accepted, allocation churn should stop within two allocation cycles (~2m)
Trent: monitoring — tailing p99: it dipped to 480ms after override, throughput recovering, eviction_count back to normal
Li: follow-up: we should still capture heap/profile from the noisy host (44b). Uploading perf trace to /tmp/44b-kernelfallback-1719002022.svg
Jenna: can someone grab kernel selection logs and batching window histograms for last 30m? Need to correlate batch size collapse with KV miss storm
Maya: grabbing them now. snippet from batching metric: `batch_size.p50 4 -> 1.2` and `batch_wait_ms.p95 120 -> 410` during spike
Trent: that matches fallback kernel path — smaller batches because slower kernels increase per-token latency, batching heuristic gives up
Li: root cause hypothesis: lowered affinity increased inter-host migrations which exposed a host with degraded kernel/caching behavior; that host's KV cache miss storm caused cache evictions, causing small batch sizes and kernel selection thrash, cascading into latency and throughput drop
Jenna: action items: 1) keep placement override until affinity change is reverted, 2) revert affinity_weight PR, 3) deep-dive noisy host 44b (kernel drivers / nvml counters / mem errors), 4) add alert for kernel-selection-thrashing and batch_size collapse
Maya: agree. I've filed a follow-up incident ticket INC-171900-oscillate with the above actions and timeline. tagging infra and eng-runtime for deep-dive
Trent: also recommend a short-term scheduler tweak: when batch_size.p50 < 2 for >1m escalate host as 'degraded' so we avoid routing to it automatically
Li: copied logs and perf artifacts to the incident folder. I'll take 44b for forensic tomorrow. For now, keep overrides active and notify cust-teamX about degraded window
Jenna: sending customer notification draft now. ops-bot: post scheduled status update in 10m
ops-bot: status update posted to #statuspage (incident INC-171900-oscillate)
Maya: thanks all — monitoring continues, will update when rollback completes or if we see regression
Trent: rolling back affinity PR now (queued). ETA 8m for full effect on placement decisions
Maya: last check: p99 steady at ~420ms, throughput back to 96% baseline. closing immediate mitigation — keeping ticket open for postmortem and perf regression fix
Jenna: adding postmortem owners: jenna (prod), li (infra), trent (runtime).
Maya: end of thread.
